# Lab 3 `results/runs.jsonl` record schema

Every command (`train`, `eval`, `bench`) appends exactly one JSON object per
attempted run to `results/runs.jsonl` (append-only: lines are never edited or
deleted; a corrected re-bench adds a new line whose `supersedes` lists the
earlier, now-incorrect run_ids). This file documents the fields.

## Identity / linkage

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | str | Unique id for this record: `<arch>-<method>-<UTC timestamp>-<shortuuid>`. |
| `status` | str | `"ok"` or `"failed"`. |
| `reason` | str/null | Failure reason when `status == "failed"`. |
| `part` | str | `"A"` (dense reference). |
| `phase` | str/null | Matrix phase the record belongs to: `"pilot"` for the Part B pilot matrix (seed 0, including the B.6 `dense_ft` control arms) and `"confirm"` for the confirmatory reruns (seeds 1/2/3, B.3). **B2 (2026-11-09, before any pilot-matrix run):** every new Part B record carries `phase`; all earlier records (Part A, and the B1/B1b Part B smoke rows) predate the field and carry `null` in any record written by new code, or no field at all (never edited — the log is append-only). |
| `architecture` | str | `mlp` / `cnn` / `gcn`. |
| `method` | str | `"dense"` for the Part A baseline. |
| `seed` | int | Random seed. |
| `command` | str | `train` / `eval` / `bench`. |
| `parent_run_id` | str/null | For `bench` (and `eval`), the `run_id` of the **training run** that produced the checkpoint being benchmarked. Carried from the checkpoint metadata `run_id`. |
| `supersedes` | list[str] | For a corrected re-bench: the `run_id`s of the earlier bench records for the same (architecture, seed) that are now known to be incorrect (e.g. A1's wrong MAC/byte figures). The old lines remain in the log untouched. |

## Training / selection

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `train_epochs` | int/null | Epochs actually run (may stop early). |
| `finetune_epochs` | int | 0 in Part A. |
| `best_epoch` | int/null | Epoch of the validation-selected checkpoint. |
| `val_acc`, `val_loss` | float/null | Validation accuracy / loss. |
| `test_acc` | float/null | Test accuracy (evaluated only on the selected checkpoint). |

## Size

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `total_params` | int | `sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())`. |
| `nonzero_params` | int | Number of nonzero weight/param elements. For the dense baseline this equals `total_params`; Part B arms report the physically sparse count. |
| `dense_bytes` | int | **Actual on-disk size** (bytes) of a `torch.save(state_dict)` file — the bare state dict (no metadata) written to a temp file, read with `os.path.getsize`. Includes the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead, so it is slightly larger than `raw_tensor_bytes`. |
| `raw_tensor_bytes` | int | `sum(t.numel() * t.element_size())` over every state_dict tensor — pure payload bytes, no container overhead. |
| `gzip_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** gzip-9 size (bytes) of the `dense_bytes` state_dict file. Reported for **every run, dense included** — it is a property of the dense container, not of a compression method. Null only where a run failed before measuring it. |
| `compressed_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** RESERVED for the **compact-export artifact** (Part B path 2: the genuinely sparse on-disk file — S2 rebuilt dense model, S1/S3 CSR file, S4 packed N:M file). **Null for the dense Part A baseline** (dense has no compact export). Part A `bench` rows record the gzip-9 figure in `gzip_bytes`, not here. |

### Part B (sparsity) additions (Task B1)

Pruning arms (`command == "prune"`, `part == "B"`) append **two rows per arm**,
`stage="post_prune"` and `stage="post_finetune"`, sharing one `arm_id`.
(The pilot driver `uv run python -m lab3 pilot` appends exactly these rows with
`phase="pilot"`, seed 0, one per cell of {mlp,cnn,gcn} x {s1,s2,s3,s4} x
===
# Figure captions

- fig acc_vs_sparsity.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero, -); y: test accuracy (-). One line per method (color = method): dashed = post_prune, solid = post_finetune, seed-0 pilot (results/pilot_summary.csv, phase=pilot rows). Open P markers: confirmatory points, mean +/- sample std of test_acc over seeds 1-3 (results/confirm_summary.csv, stage=post_finetune). Horizontal reference lines (labeled in the shared legend, not on the plot): black = dense seed-0 test acc, gray = dense seed-0 val acc (results/baselines.md, Part A train seed-0); dotted black = dense_ft seed-0 (pilot). Source: results/pilot_summary.csv, results/confirm_summary.csv, results/baselines.md.
- fig latency_vs_accuracy.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: median forward latency of each runtime path, batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN (ms, log scale), from the per-path timing blocks of results/pilot_summary.csv (phase=pilot, stage=post_finetune, seed-0: {path}_batch_256_median_ms / {path}_full_graph_median_ms); y: post_finetune test accuracy (-). One hollow marker per arm for the dense_zeros path and one filled marker for the compact path; marker shape = method (o s1, s s2, ^ s3, D s4) — 32 points per panel. Black star: dense seed-0 (results/baselines.md, Part A bench seed-0). Source: results/pilot_summary.csv, results/baselines.md.
- fig size_vs_sparsity.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero, -); y: bytes on disk (log scale). One series per method (color = method) and artifact type (line style = artifact): solid = dense_zeros path (dense_bytes, zeros still stored), dashed = gzip-9 of the dense state_dict (gzip_bytes), dash-dot = compact artifact (compressed_bytes; S2 rebuilt dense / S1,S3 CSR / S4 packed N:M). Black line: dense on-disk bytes (results/baselines.md, Part A bench seed-0). All byte values > 1000 B (asserted). Source: results/pilot_summary.csv (phase=pilot, stage=post_finetune rows: dense_bytes / gzip_bytes / compressed_bytes) and results/baselines.md.

## Part C precision

- fig partC_precision_valacc.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: reduced-precision format; y: validation accuracy (-). 5 formats: fp16, bf16, int8_dynamic (qnnpack), int8_static (qnnpack FX), int4_simulated. Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, status=ok (val_acc). One bar per format per architecture.
- fig partC_precision_latency.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: format; y: median forward latency (log scale, ms). Batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN (frozen bench protocol). Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, status=ok (latency). One bar per format per architecture.
- fig partC_precision_frac_macs.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: format; y: fraction of total forward MACs performed in reduced precision (-). For half formats all ops are reduced (1.0); for INT8 the fraction is the qnnpack-quantized ops (1.0 for MLP, 1.0 for GCN projections, 0.5 for CNN where Conv2d stays fp32); INT4 simulated is 0.0 (fp32 dequant inside timed region). Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, status=ok (frac_macs_reduced_precision, per_layer).

## Part C (C2) size-latency

- fig precision_size_latency.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: artifact bytes (log); y: median forward latency (log, ms; batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN). One point per format. Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, status=ok, python 3.12 (C2 run). All 5 formats present for all architectures.

## Part C (C2) factorial

- fig factorial.png: 3x3 grid (rows = metric: validation accuracy, artifact bytes, median latency; columns = MLP/CNN/GCN). One bar per condition: dense_fp32, sparse_fp32, dense_int8, sparse_int8 (the C2-selected INT8 method applied to dense and to the sparse operating point). Bytes and latency on log scale. Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=factorial, status=ok, python 3.12 (C2 run).
===

# (main() invocation moved to the single __main__ block at the bottom)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# C2: precision_size_latency + factorial figures
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _c2_rows(recs: list[dict], phase: str) -> dict[tuple[str, str], dict]:
    """Latest C2-run ok row per (architecture, method).

    C2 reran the entire Part C study on the pinned Python 3.12 environment. The
    C1b rows (Python 3.13) were superseded; C2 rows are the ones whose `code`
    hash and python version match the C2 run. We select the LATEST (file order)
    ok row per (arch, method) whose python is 3.12.x — the C2 environment.
    """
    out: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    for r in recs:
        if r.get("part") != "C" or r.get("phase") != phase or r.get("status") != "ok":
            continue
        py = (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "")
        if not py.startswith("3.12"):
            continue  # skip C1b (3.13) superseded rows
        out[(r["architecture"], r["method"])] = r  # latest wins
    return out


def precision_size_latency() -> None:
    """C2 item 8a: figures/precision_size_latency.png. Per arch: artifact bytes
    vs batch-256 / full-graph median latency, one point per format, log axes,
    unsupported formats listed in the caption. Keeps the existing valacc/
    latency/frac_macs figures (separate files)."""
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prec = _c2_rows(recs, "precision")
    if not prec:
        print("no C2 phase=precision rows; skipping precision_size_latency")
        return

    def lat(r: dict) -> float | None:
        v = (r.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[r["architecture"]]) or {}
        m = v.get("median_ms")
        return float(m) if isinstance(m, (int, float)) and m > 0 else None

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
    captions: list[str] = []
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        xs, ys, labels, colors = [], [], [], []
        for j, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS):
            r = prec.get((arch, fmt))
            if r is None:
                continue
            ab = r.get("artifact_bytes")
            lv = lat(r)
            if not ab or lv is None:
                continue
            xs.append(ab); ys.append(lv)
            labels.append(FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]); colors.append(fmt)
        if xs:
            ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=60, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i) for i in range(len(xs))],
                       zorder=3, edgecolors="k", linewidths=0.5)
            for xi, yi, lb in zip(xs, ys, labels):
                ax.annotate(lb, (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",
                            xytext=(4, 4), fontsize=7)
            ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log")
            ax.set_xlabel("artifact bytes (log)")
            ax.set_ylabel("median latency (log, ms)")
            ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")
        else:
            ax.axis("off")
        ax.set_title(arch.upper())
    # unsupported formats (not present for some arch) -> caption
    missing = []
    for arch in ARCHS:
        for fmt in PRECISION_FORMATS:
            if (arch, fmt) not in prec:
                missing.append(f"{arch}/{fmt}")
    _shared_legend(
        fig,
        [_h(plt.cm.tab10(i), FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]) for i, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS)],
        title="format", ncol=5, pad=0.10,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.12, 1, 1))
    _tight_savefig(fig, FIGURES / "precision_size_latency.png", dpi=150)
    cap = ("fig precision_size_latency.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: artifact bytes "
           "(log); y: median forward latency (log, ms; batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph "
           "for GCN). One point per format. Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, "
           "phase=precision, status=ok, python 3.12 (C2 run). "
           + ("Unsupported/absent formats (not plotted): " + ", ".join(missing) + "."
              if missing else "All 5 formats present for all architectures."))
    captions.append(cap)
    plt.close(fig)

    cap_path = FIGURES / "CAPTIONS.md"
    with open(cap_path, "a") as f:
        f.write("\n## Part C (C2) size-latency\n\n")
        for c in captions:
            f.write("- " + c + "\n")

def _c2_rows(recs: list[dict], phase: str) -> dict[tuple[str, str], dict]:
    """Latest C2-run ok row per (architecture, method).

    C2 reran the entire Part C study on the pinned Python 3.12 environment. The
    C1b rows (Python 3.13) were superseded; C2 rows are the ones whose `code`
    hash and python version match the C2 run. We select the LATEST (file order)
    ok row per (arch, method) whose python is 3.12.x — the C2 environment.
    """
    out: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    for r in recs:
        if r.get("part") != "C" or r.get("phase") != phase or r.get("status") != "ok":
            continue
        py = (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "")
        if not py.startswith("3.12"):
            continue  # skip C1b (3.13) superseded rows
        out[(r["architecture"], r["method"])] = r  # latest wins
    return out

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "code")
import torch
torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from lab3 import precision as P
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
import json
sel = json.load(open("results/partc_selection.json"))

def scan(m, label):
    print("=====", label)
    # walk named_modules and inspect instance attrs (not in _parameters/_buffers)
    for n, mod in m.named_modules():
        # params (non-recursive)
        for k, p in mod.named_parameters(recurse=False):
            print(f"  PARAM {n or '<root>'}.{k} {p.dtype} {tuple(p.shape)}")
        for k, b in mod.named_buffers(recurse=False):
            print(f"  BUFFER {n or '<root>'}.{k} {b.dtype} {tuple(b.shape)}")
        for k, v in list(vars(mod).items()):
            if k.startswith("_") and k not in ("_parameters", "_buffers", "_modules",
                                               "_non_persistent_buffers_set",
                                               "_backward_pre_hooks", "_backward_hooks",
                                               "_forward_hooks", "_forward_hooks_always_called",
                                               "_forward_pre_hooks", "_forward_pre_hooks_always_called",
                                               "_state_dict_hooks", "_state_dict_pre_hooks",
                                               "_load_state_dict_pre_hooks", "_load_state_dict_post_hooks",
                                               "_is_full_backward_hook"):
                if torch.is_tensor(v) or isinstance(v, torch.ScriptObject):
                    print(f"  RAWATTR {n or '<root>'}.{k} {type(v).__name__} {tuple(v.shape) if torch.is_tensor(v) else ''}")
    # full model state dict
    sd = m.state_dict()
    print("  --- state_dict keys ---")
    for k, v in sd.items():
        if torch.is_tensor(v):
            print(f"  SD {k} {v.dtype} {tuple(v.shape)} {v.numel()*v.element_size()}B")
        else:
            print(f"  SD {k} {type(v).__name__}")

parent,_ = load_checkpoint("mlp",0); parent.eval()
m,_ = P.int8_quantize_static(parent, "mlp")
scan(m, "mlp static")
m2,_ = P.int8_quantize_static(parent, "mlp")
print()
print("int8_nonzero:", P.int8_nonzero(m2), "bytes_by_dtype:", P.bytes_by_dtype(m2, "int8_static"))

import sys

def scan(m, label):
    print("=====", label)
    for n, mod in m.named_modules():
        for k, p in mod.named_parameters(recurse=False):
            print(f"  PARAM {n or '<root>'}.{k} {p.dtype} {tuple(p.shape)}")
        for k, b in mod.named_buffers(recurse=False):
            print(f"  BUFFER {n or '<root>'}.{k} {b.dtype} {tuple(b.shape)}")
        for k, v in list(vars(mod).items()):
            if k.startswith("_") and k not in ("_parameters", "_buffers", "_modules",

                                               "_backward_pre_hooks", "_backward_hooks",
                                               "_forward_hooks", "_forward_hooks_always_called",
                                               "_forward_pre_hooks", "_forward_pre_hooks_always_called",
                                               "_state_dict_hooks", "_state_dict_pre_hooks",
                                               "_load_state_dict_pre_hooks", "_load_state_dict_post_hooks",
                                               "_is_full_backward_hook"):
                if torch.is_tensor(v) or isinstance(v, torch.ScriptObject):
                    print(f"  RAWATTR {n or '<root>'}.{k} {type(v).__name__} {tuple(v.shape) if torch.is_tensor(v) else ''}")
    print("  --- state_dict keys ---")
    for k, v in m.state_dict().items():
        if torch.is_tensor(v):
            print(f"  SD {k} {v.dtype} {tuple(v.shape)} {v.numel()*v.element_size()}B")

m2,_ = P.int8_quantize_static(parent, "gcn")
scan(m2, "gcn static (dense parent)")

w2, b2 = pp._weight_bias()
print("via _weight_bias:", w2.dtype, tuple(w2.shape), b2.dtype, tuple(b2.shape))

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "code")
import torch
torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from lab3 import precision as P
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
import json
sel8 = json.load(open("results/int8_selection.json"))["selection"]
sel = json.load(open("results/partc_selection.json"))

def parent_weights(arch, sparse=False):
    if sparse:
        m,_ = P._load_sparse_checkpoint(arch, sel[arch]["selected"]["pilot_arm_id"])
    else:
        m,_ = load_checkpoint(arch,0)
    m.eval()
    tot=0
    for n,op,k in P.eligible_ops(m):
        w = getattr(op,'weight',None)
        if w is not None:
            tot += int(w.count_nonzero())
    return tot

for arch in ("mlp","cnn","gcn"):
    pw_d = parent_weights(arch, False); pw_s = parent_weights(arch, True)
    for lbl, pw, loader in (("dense", pw_d, lambda: load_checkpoint(arch,0)),
                            ("sparse", pw_s, lambda: P._load_sparse_checkpoint(arch, sel[arch]["selected"]["pilot_arm_id"]))):
        src,_ = loader(); src.eval()
        for name, q in (("dyn", P.int8_quantize_dynamic), ("stat", P.int8_quantize_static)):
            m,_ = q(src, arch)
            bbd = P.bytes_by_dtype(m, name)
            nnz = P.int8_nonzero(m)
            ok = "OK" if (bbd.get("int8",0) >= pw and 0.8*nnz <= pw <= 1.2*nnz) else "FAIL"
            print(f"{arch} {name:4s} {lbl}: bbd={bbd} nnz={nnz} parent_w_nnz={pw}  {ok}")

import torch
torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from lab3 import precision as P
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
import json

# What does _int_weight_tensors currently find per arch/method (dense)?
for arch in ("mlp","cnn","gcn"):
    parent,_ = load_checkpoint(arch,0); parent.eval()
    sparse,_ = P._load_sparse_checkpoint(arch, sel[arch]["selected"]["pilot_arm_id"])

            ts = P._int_weight_tensors(m)
            print(f"{arch} {name} {lbl}: tensors={[(tuple(t.shape), int(t.count_nonzero())) for t in ts]}")

        for k, v in list(vars(mod).items()):
            if isinstance(v, torch.ScriptObject):
                try:

        if not torch.is_tensor(v):
            print(f"  SD: {k} ({type(v).__name__})")

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "code")
import torch
torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from lab3 import precision as P
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
import json
sel8 = json.load(open("results/int8_selection.json"))["selection"]

# For each arch+method, what does bytes_by_dtype report, and what are the eligible
# weight numel / fp32-nnz of the quantized layers (dense + sparse parents)?
def eligible(model):
    out = []
    for n, op, k in P.eligible_ops(model):
        if k == "lin":
            op = getattr(op, "lin", op)
        w = getattr(op, "weight", None)
        if w is not None:
            out.append((n, int(w.numel()), int(w.count_nonzero())))
    return out

for arch in ("mlp","cnn","gcn"):
    parent,_ = load_checkpoint(arch,0); parent.eval()
    epar = eligible(parent)
    print("===", arch, "eligible parent:", epar)
    for name, q in (("int8_dynamic", P.int8_quantize_dynamic), ("int8_static", P.int8_quantize_static)):
        m,_ = q(parent, arch)
        bbd = P.bytes_by_dtype(m, name)
        nnz = P.int8_nonzero(m)
        print(f"   {name}: bbd={bbd} int8_nonzero={nnz}")

def _qnnpack_weight_bias(mod: nn.Module) -> tuple | None:
    """(qint8 weight, fp32 bias|None) for a qnnpack quantized op, or None.

    C3: handles both qnnpack shapes the study produces:
      (a) dynamic / FX-static linears and convs wrapped as modules with a
          `_packed_params` LinearPackedParams child (`_weight_bias()` works
          through the Python wrapper, including CNN static's fused
          ConvReLU2d / Conv2d); and
      (b) FX-static GCN per-projection GraphModules, where `convert_fx` lifts
          the packed weight to a raw instance attribute `_packed_weight_N`
          (`torch.ScriptObject` of class `torch.classes.quantized.
          LinearPackedParamsBase`, whose C++ binding exposes `unpack()` but
          NOT `_weight_bias`). C2's traversal only handled (a) via the
          module-level `_packed_params` check, so the GCN static INT8 rows
          (and the dense/sparse variants of the CNN static conv weights)
          were invisible: `nonzero_after_int8` counted the 16+7 GCN biases
          (23) and `bytes_by_dtype` showed `{"fp32": 92}` for the whole
          quantized projection.
    """
    pp = getattr(mod, "_packed_params", None)
    if pp is not None and not isinstance(pp, torch.ScriptObject):
        try:
            qw, bias = pp._weight_bias()
            if torch.is_tensor(qw) and qw.dtype in (torch.qint8, torch.quint8):
                return qw, bias
        except Exception:
            pass
        return None  # has a Python packed-params child: no raw ScriptObject fallback
    for k, v in list(vars(mod).items()):
        if not isinstance(v, torch.ScriptObject):
            continue
        try:
            parts = v.unpack()  # (qint8 weight, [bias]) — LinearPackedParamsBase
        except Exception:
            continue
        if (len(parts) >= 1 and torch.is_tensor(parts[0])

def _is_packed_params_wrapper(mod: nn.Module) -> bool:
    """True for the Python `LinearPackedParams` wrapper module (or any module
    whose own `vars()` holds a raw packed-params ScriptObject under a
    `_packed_params` key): the integer weight is accounted once, via the
    owning op module, and the wrapper must not be visited again (its vars()
    contain the very same ScriptObject)."""
    pp = vars(mod).get("_packed_params")
    return isinstance(pp, torch.ScriptObject)


def _int_weight_tensors(model: nn.Module) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
    """Return the integer weight tensors of a converted model, unpacking
    qnnpack packed params (int_repr) and INT4 packed buffers, so that nonzero
    counts / byte accounting operate on the *integer* representation rather
    than on fp32 placeholders. FP16/BF16/FP32 models have no integer weight
    representation and yield an empty list. C3: also finds the FX-static
    GraphModule `_packed_weight_N` ScriptObjects (see `_qnnpack_weight_bias`)."""
    out: list[torch.Tensor] = []
    for _name, mod in model.named_modules():
        if isinstance(mod, (Int4PackedLinear, Int4PackedConv)):
            # Packed 2-values-per-uint8 buffer; report it as its own dtype.
            out.append(mod.packed)
            continue
        if _is_packed_params_wrapper(mod):
            continue
        wb = _qnnpack_weight_bias(mod)
        if wb is not None:
            out.append(wb[0].int_repr())
    return out

@pytest.mark.parametrize("arch", ["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
def test_int8_nonzero_not_zero(arch, threads, checkpoints):
    """C2 item 5: nonzero count of the integer weight representation is nonzero
    for dense INT8 (the old code reported 0 for every INT8 row because it counted
    fp32 placeholder params)."""
    parent, _ = checkpoints[arch]
    parent.eval()
    model, _ = P.int8_quantize_dynamic(parent, arch)
    nnz = P.int8_nonzero(model)
    parent_weight_nnz = sum(int(m.weight.count_nonzero())
                            for _n, m, _k in P.eligible_ops(parent))
    assert nnz > 0, f"{arch} INT8 dynamic integer nonzero count is 0"
    # Dense parent weights are all nonzero; per-tensor symmetric int8 quantization
    # (0 -> 0) zeros out small-magnitude weights that fall within half a quant
    # step. The integer-representation nonzero count must be a substantial
    # majority (>= 80%) of the dense parent's nonzero weights — this is the
    # signal that the count is the real integer-representation count, not the
    # broken 0 the C1b code reported.
    assert nnz >= 0.8 * parent_weight_nnz, (
        f"{arch} INT8 dynamic nnz {nnz} < 80% of parent weight nnz {parent_weight_nnz}"
    )

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "code")
import torch
torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from lab3 import precision as P
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
import json
sel = json.load(open("results/partc_selection.json"))

# What does the CNN static conv1 module look like?
parent,_ = load_checkpoint("cnn",0); parent.eval()
m,_ = P.int8_quantize_static(parent, "cnn")
c1 = dict(m.named_modules())["conv1"]
print("conv1 type:", type(c1).__name__)
pp = getattr(c1, "_packed_params", None)
print("pp type:", type(pp).__name__)
print("pp is ScriptObject:", isinstance(pp, torch.ScriptObject))
wb = P._qnnpack_weight_bias(c1)
print("wb:", None if wb is None else (tuple(wb[0].shape), wb[1].dtype if wb[1] is not None else None))
print("conv1 named_buffers:", {k: (str(v.dtype), tuple(v.shape)) for k, v in c1.named_buffers()})
print("conv1 named_parameters:", {k: (str(v.dtype), tuple(v.shape)) for k, v in c1.named_parameters()})
# check _is_packed_params_wrapper
print("is wrapper:", P._is_packed_params_wrapper(c1))

# also gcn dyn
gp,_ = load_checkpoint("gcn",0); gp.eval()
m,_ = P.int8_quantize_dynamic(gp, "gcn")
lin = dict(m.named_modules())["conv1.lin"]
print("gcn dyn conv1.lin type:", type(lin).__name__)
wb = P._qnnpack_weight_bias(lin)
print("wb:", None if wb is None else (tuple(wb[0].shape),))
print("is wrapper:", P._is_packed_params_wrapper(lin))

edits.oldText:
def _qnnpack_weight_bias(mod: nn.Module) -> tuple | None:
    """(qint8 weight, fp32 bias|None) for a qnnpack quantized op, or None.

    C3: handles both qnnpack shapes the study produces:
      (a) dynamic / FX-static linears and convs wrapped as modules with a
          `_packed_params` LinearPackedParams child (`_weight_bias()` works
          through the Python wrapper, including CNN static's fused
          ConvReLU2d / Conv2d); and
      (b) FX-static GCN per-projection GraphModules, where `convert_fx` lifts
          the packed weight to a raw instance attribute `_packed_weight_N`
          (`torch.ScriptObject` of class `torch.classes.quantized.
          LinearPackedParamsBase`, whose C++ binding exposes `unpack()` but
          NOT `_weight_bias`). C2's traversal only handled (a) via the
          module-level `_packed_params` check, so the GCN static INT8 rows
          (and the dense/sparse variants of the CNN static conv weights)
          were invisible: `nonzero_after_int8` counted the 16+7 GCN biases
          (23) and `bytes_by_dtype` showed `{"fp32": 92}` for the whole
          quantized projection.
    """
    pp = getattr(mod, "_packed_params", None)
    if pp is not None and not isinstance(pp, torch.ScriptObject):
        # Python LinearPackedParams wrapper: the raw ScriptObject lives in
        # THIS module's vars() under the same key, so it must not also be
        # picked up by the raw-attribute scan below (double count).
        try:
            qw, bias = pp._weight_bias()
            if torch.is_tensor(qw) and qw.dtype in (torch.qint8, torch.quint8):
                return qw, bias
        except Exception:
            pass
        return None  # has a Python packed-params child: done here
    for k, v in list(vars(mod).items()):
        if not isinstance(v, torch.ScriptObject):
            continue
        try:
            parts = v.unpack()  # (qint8 weight, [bias]) — LinearPackedParamsBase
        except Exception:
            continue
        if (len(parts) >= 1 and torch.is_tensor(parts[0])
                and parts[0].dtype in (torch.qint8, torch.quint8)):
            return parts[0], (parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 and torch.is_tensor(parts[1])
                              else None)
    return None

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "code")
import torch
torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
from lab3 import precision as P
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint

# Which modules does _qnnpack_weight_bias hit for each arch/method?
for arch in ("mlp","cnn","gcn"):
    parent,_ = load_checkpoint(arch,0); parent.eval()
    for name, q in (("dyn", P.int8_quantize_dynamic), ("stat", P.int8_quantize_static)):
        m,_ = q(parent, arch)
        hits = []
        for n, mod in m.named_modules():
            if P._is_packed_params_wrapper(mod):
                hits.append((n or "<root>", "WRAPPER-SKIP"))
                continue
            wb = P._qnnpack_weight_bias(mod)
            if wb is not None:
                hits.append((n or "<root>", type(mod).__name__, tuple(wb[0].shape), int(wb[0].numel())))
        print(arch, name, hits)
EOF

@pytest.mark.parametrize("arch", ["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
def test_int8_nonzero_not_zero(arch, threads, checkpoints):
    """C2 item 5: nonzero count of the integer weight representation is nonzero
    for dense INT8 (the old code reported 0 for every INT8 row because it counted
    fp32 placeholder params)."""
    parent, _ = checkpoints[arch]
    parent.eval()
    model, _ = P.int8_quantize_dynamic(parent, arch)
    nnz = P.int8_nonzero(model)
    parent_weight_nnz = sum(int(m.weight.count_nonzero())
                            for _n, m, _k in P.eligible_ops(parent))
    assert nnz > 0, f"{arch} INT8 dynamic integer nonzero count is 0"
    # Dense parent weights are all nonzero; per-tensor symmetric int8 quantization
    # (0 -> 0) zeros out small-magnitude weights that fall within half a quant
    # step. The integer-representation nonzero count must be a substantial
    # majority (>= 80%) of the dense parent's nonzero weights — this is the
    # signal that the count is the real integer-representation count, not the
    # broken 0 the C1b code reported.
    assert nnz >= 0.8 * parent_weight_nnz, (
        f"{arch} INT8 dynamic nnz {nnz} < 80% of parent weight nnz {parent_weight_nnz}"
    )

@pytest.mark.parametrize("fmt", ["fp16", "bf16", "int8_dynamic", "int8_static", "int4_simulated"])
def test_bytes_by_dtype_present(arch, fmt, threads, checkpoints):
    """C2 item 4: bytes_by_dtype is a non-empty per-dtype dict on every row, and
    its sum (payload_bytes) is <= artifact_bytes (container overhead is the
    difference, visible to the reader)."""
    parent, _ = checkpoints[arch]
    parent.eval()
    if fmt in ("fp16", "bf16"):
        model = P.half_quantize(parent, arch,
                                torch.float16 if fmt == "fp16" else torch.bfloat16)
    elif fmt == "int8_dynamic":
        model, _ = P.int8_quantize_dynamic(parent, arch)
    elif fmt == "int8_static":
        model, _ = P.int8_quantize_static(parent, arch)
    else:
        model = P.int4_quantize(parent, arch)
    bbd = P.bytes_by_dtype(model, fmt)
    assert isinstance(bbd, dict) and len(bbd) > 0, f"{arch} {fmt}: empty bytes_by_dtype"
    assert all(v > 0 for v in bbd.values()), f"{arch} {fmt}: non-positive byte entry"
    # artifact_bytes >= payload_bytes (container overhead >= 0)
    import tempfile, pathlib
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        path = pathlib.Path(d) / f"{arch}_{fmt}.pt"
        ab = P._save_artifact(model, path, fmt, arch)
    assert ab >= int(sum(bbd.values())), (
        f"{arch} {fmt}: artifact_bytes {ab} < payload_bytes {sum(bbd.values())}"
    )

def test_int8_bytes_count_quantized_weights(arch, fmt, threads, checkpoints):
    """C3: for every INT8 artifact of every arch, the integer-weight accounting
    must actually see the quantized projection weights.

    C2's traversal (`_int_weight_tensors` / `bytes_by_dtype`) only matched
    modules whose `_packed_params` child exposed a working `_weight_bias()`,
    so it MISSED the FX-static shape where `convert_fx` attaches the packed
    weight as a raw `torch.ScriptObject` attribute (`_packed_weight_N` on the
    GCN per-projection GraphModules; `_packed_params` on the CNN static convs).

    `nonzero_after_int8 = 23` (the 16+7 GCN biases, not the 22,928+112
    projection weights) and `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}` (biases only),
    even though val acc (0.794-0.796) proved the INT8 weights were present.

    Asserts (dense parent, both INT8 methods, all 3 archs). "Quantized layers"
    = the eligible ops actually converted to qnnpack int8 (both methods
    quantize every eligible op, except the frozen C.1 dynamic spec
    `quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear})` leaves CNN Conv2d in fp32):
      * `bytes_by_dtype["int8"]` >= the number of weights of the quantized
        layers (1 B/elem payload, so byte count == weight count);
      * `int8_nonzero` (int_repr nonzero count) is within 20% of the fp32
        nonzero count of those same layers — per-tensor symmetric INT8
        (0 -> 0) zeros out at most a small fraction of small-magnitude
        weights, so a correct count must track the fp32 nonzero count.
    """

    parent.eval()
    maker = (P.int8_quantize_dynamic if fmt == "int8_dynamic"
             else P.int8_quantize_static)
    model, _ = maker(parent, arch)

    # Which eligible ops actually got quantized (int8)?
    conv_by_name = {n: m for n, m in model.named_modules()}
    quantized_numel = 0
    quantized_fp32_nnz = 0
    for n, op, k in P.eligible_ops(parent):
        w = getattr(op, "weight", None)
        if w is None:
            continue
        qmod = conv_by_name.get(n)
        is_int8 = (
            (k in ("linear", "lin") and (qmod is not None
                                         and P._qnnpack_weight_bias(qmod) is not None))
            or (k == "conv" and qmod is not None
                and P._is_qnnpack_quantized_conv(qmod))
        )
        if is_int8:
            quantized_numel += int(w.numel())
            quantized_fp32_nnz += int(w.count_nonzero())

        f"{arch} {fmt}: no eligible op detected as quantized?"

    bbd = P.bytes_by_dtype(model, fmt)
    nnz = P.int8_nonzero(model)

    # (1 B/elem, so bytes == element count for the int8 weight tensors).
    assert bbd.get("int8", 0) >= quantized_numel, (
        f"{arch} {fmt}: bytes_by_dtype['int8']={bbd.get('int8')} < "
        f"quantized-layer weights {quantized_numel} "
        f"(int8 payload missing quantized weights)"
    )
    # The int_repr nonzero count must track the fp32 nonzero count of the
    # quantized layers within 20% (quantization can only zero out small
    # weights; it cannot invent or erase most of them).
    assert 0.8 * quantized_fp32_nnz <= nnz <= 1.2 * quantized_fp32_nnz, (

def test_int8_bytes_count_quantized_weights(arch, fmt, threads, checkpoints):
    """C3: for every INT8 artifact of every arch, the integer-weight accounting
    must actually see the quantized projection weights.

    C2's traversal (`_int_weight_tensors` / `bytes_by_dtype`) only matched
    modules whose `_packed_params` child exposed a working `_weight_bias()`,
    so it MISSED the FX-static shape where `convert_fx` attaches the packed
    weight as a raw `torch.ScriptObject` attribute (`_packed_weight_N` on the
    GCN per-projection GraphModules; `_packed_params` on the CNN static convs).
    Symptom in C2: gcn dense/sparse int8 reported
    `nonzero_after_int8 = 23` (the 16+7 GCN biases, not the 22,928+112
    projection weights) and `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}` (biases only),
    even though val acc (0.794-0.796) proved the INT8 weights were present.

    Asserts (dense parent, both INT8 methods, all 3 archs):
      * `bytes_by_dtype["int8"]` >= the total number of weights in the
        quantized layers (1 B/elem payload, so byte count == weight count);
      * `int8_nonzero` (int_repr nonzero count) is within 20% of the fp32
        nonzero count of those same layers — per-tensor symmetric INT8
        (0 -> 0) zeros out at most a small fraction of small-magnitude
        weights, so a correct count must track the fp32 nonzero count.
    """
    parent, _ = checkpoints[arch]
    parent.eval()
    maker = (P.int8_quantize_dynamic if fmt == "int8_dynamic"
             else P.int8_quantize_static)
    model, _ = maker(parent, arch)

    # fp32 nonzero count of the quantized layers (eligible ops = the layers the
    # converter quantizes; every eligible op IS quantized under both methods).
    fp32_nnz = 0
    eligible_numel = 0
    for _n, op, _k in P.eligible_ops(parent):
        op = getattr(op, "lin", op)  # GCNConv -> its .lin projection
        w = getattr(op, "weight", None)
        if w is not None:
            fp32_nnz += int(w.count_nonzero())
            eligible_numel += int(w.numel())
    assert fp32_nnz > 0 and eligible_numel > 0, \
        f"{arch}: no eligible weights to quantize?"

    bbd = P.bytes_by_dtype(model, fmt)
    nnz = P.int8_nonzero(model)

    # The int8 payload must cover every weight of the quantized layers
    # (1 B/elem, so bytes == element count for the int8 weight tensors).
    assert bbd.get("int8", 0) >= eligible_numel, (
        f"{arch} {fmt}: bytes_by_dtype['int8']={bbd.get('int8')} < "
        f"eligible quantized-layer weights {eligible_numel} "
        f"(int8 payload missing quantized weights)"
    )
    # The int_repr nonzero count must track the fp32 nonzero count of those
    # layers within 20% (quantization can only zero out small weights; it
    # cannot invent or erase most of them).
    assert 0.8 * fp32_nnz <= nnz <= 1.2 * fp32_nnz, (
        f"{arch} {fmt}: int8_nonzero {nnz} not within 20% of fp32 nonzero "
        f"count {fp32_nnz} of the quantized layers"
    )

@pytest.mark.parametrize("arch", ["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("fmt", ["int8_dynamic", "int8_static"])
def test_int8_bytes_count_quantized_weights(arch, fmt, threads, checkpoints):
    """C3: for every INT8 artifact of every arch, the integer-weight accounting
    must actually see the quantized projection weights.

    C2's traversal (`_int_weight_tensors` / `bytes_by_dtype`) only matched
    modules whose `_packed_params` child exposed a working `_weight_bias()`,
    so it MISSED the FX-static shape where `convert_fx` attaches the packed
    weight as a raw `torch.ScriptObject` attribute (`_packed_weight_N` on the
    GCN per-projection GraphModules; `_packed_params` on the CNN static convs).
    Symptom in C2: gcn dense/sparse int8 reported
    `nonzero_after_int8 = 23` (the 16+7 GCN biases, not the 22,928+112
    projection weights) and `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}` (biases only),
    even though val acc (0.794-0.796) proved the INT8 weights were present.

    Asserts (dense parent, both INT8 methods, all 3 archs). "Quantized layers"
    = the eligible ops actually converted to qnnpack int8 (both methods
    quantize every eligible op, except the frozen C.1 dynamic spec
    `quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear})` leaves CNN Conv2d in fp32):
      * `bytes_by_dtype["int8"]` >= the number of weights of the quantized
        layers (1 B/elem payload, so byte count == weight count);
      * `int8_nonzero` (int_repr nonzero count) is within 20% of the fp32
        nonzero count of those same layers — per-tensor symmetric INT8
        (0 -> 0) zeros out at most a small fraction of small-magnitude
        weights, so a correct count must track the fp32 nonzero count.
    """
    parent, _ = checkpoints[arch]
    parent.eval()
    maker = (P.int8_quantize_dynamic if fmt == "int8_dynamic"
             else P.int8_quantize_static)
    model, _ = maker(parent, arch)

    # Which eligible ops actually got quantized (int8)?
    conv_by_name = {n: m for n, m in model.named_modules()}
    quantized_numel = 0
    quantized_fp32_nnz = 0
    for n, op, k in P.eligible_ops(parent):
        w = getattr(op, "weight", None)
        if w is None:
            continue
        qmod = conv_by_name.get(n)
        is_int8 = (
            (k in ("linear", "lin") and (qmod is not None
                                         and P._qnnpack_weight_bias(qmod) is not None))
            or (k == "conv" and qmod is not None
                and P._is_qnnpack_quantized_conv(qmod))
        )
        if is_int8:
            quantized_numel += int(w.numel())
            quantized_fp32_nnz += int(w.count_nonzero())
    assert quantized_numel > 0 and quantized_fp32_nnz > 0, \
        f"{arch} {fmt}: no eligible op detected as quantized?"

    bbd = P.bytes_by_dtype(model, fmt)
    nnz = P.int8_nonzero(model)

    # The int8 payload must cover every weight of the quantized layers
    # (1 B/elem, so bytes == element count for the int8 weight tensors).
    assert bbd.get("int8", 0) >= quantized_numel, (
        f"{arch} {fmt}: bytes_by_dtype['int8']={bbd.get('int8')} < "
        f"quantized-layer weights {quantized_numel} "
        f"(int8 payload missing quantized weights)"
    )
    # The int_repr nonzero count must track the fp32 nonzero count of the
    # quantized layers within 20% (quantization can only zero out small
    # weights; it cannot invent or erase most of them).
    assert 0.8 * quantized_fp32_nnz <= nnz <= 1.2 * quantized_fp32_nnz, (
        f"{arch} {fmt}: int8_nonzero {nnz} not within 20% of fp32 nonzero "
        f"count {quantized_fp32_nnz} of the quantized layers"
    )

@pytest.mark.parametrize("arch", ["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("fmt", ["int8_dynamic", "int8_static"])
def test_int8_bytes_count_quantized_weights(arch, fmt, threads, checkpoints):
    """C3: for every INT8 artifact of every arch, the integer-weight accounting
    must actually see the quantized projection weights.

    C2's traversal (`_int_weight_tensors` / `bytes_by_dtype`) only matched
    modules whose `_packed_params` child exposed a working `_weight_bias()`,
    so it MISSED the FX-static shape where `convert_fx` attaches the packed
    weight as a raw `torch.ScriptObject` attribute (`_packed_weight_N` on the
    GCN per-projection GraphModules; `_packed_params` on the CNN static convs).
    Symptom in C2: gcn dense/sparse int8 reported
    `nonzero_after_int8 = 23` (the 16+7 GCN biases, not the 22,928+112
    projection weights) and `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}` (biases only),
    even though val acc (0.794-0.796) proved the INT8 weights were present.

    Asserts (dense parent, both INT8 methods, all 3 archs):
      * `bytes_by_dtype["int8"]` >= the total number of weights in the
        quantized layers (1 B/elem payload, so byte count == weight count);
      * `int8_nonzero` (int_repr nonzero count) is within 20% of the fp32
        nonzero count of those same layers — per-tensor symmetric INT8
        (0 -> 0) zeros out at most a small fraction of small-magnitude
        weights, so a correct count must track the fp32 nonzero count.
    """
    parent, _ = checkpoints[arch]
    parent.eval()
    maker = (P.int8_quantize_dynamic if fmt == "int8_dynamic"
             else P.int8_quantize_static)
    model, _ = maker(parent, arch)

    # fp32 nonzero count of the quantized layers (eligible ops = the layers the
    # converter quantizes; every eligible op IS quantized under both methods).
    fp32_nnz = 0
    eligible_numel = 0
    for _n, op, _k in P.eligible_ops(parent):
        op = getattr(op, "lin", op)  # GCNConv -> its .lin projection
        w = getattr(op, "weight", None)
        if w is not None:
            fp32_nnz += int(w.count_nonzero())
            eligible_numel += int(w.numel())
    assert fp32_nnz > 0 and eligible_numel > 0, \
        f"{arch}: no eligible weights to quantize?"

    bbd = P.bytes_by_dtype(model, fmt)
    nnz = P.int8_nonzero(model)

    # The int8 payload must cover every weight of the quantized layers
    # (1 B/elem, so bytes == element count for the int8 weight tensors).
    assert bbd.get("int8", 0) >= eligible_numel, (
        f"{arch} {fmt}: bytes_by_dtype['int8']={bbd.get('int8')} < "
        f"eligible quantized-layer weights {eligible_numel} "
        f"(int8 payload missing quantized weights)"
    )
    # The int_repr nonzero count must track the fp32 nonzero count of those
    # layers within 20% (quantization can only zero out small weights; it
    # cannot invent or erase most of them).
    assert 0.8 * fp32_nnz <= nnz <= 1.2 * fp32_nnz, (
        f"{arch} {fmt}: int8_nonzero {nnz} not within 20% of fp32 nonzero "
        f"count {fp32_nnz} of the quantized layers"
    )

out.append("the `state['pickled']` bytes embedded in it (torch.save(model) re-archives the\n")

        osz = os.path.getsize(p)
        payload = torch.load(p, weights_only=False)
        st = payload["state"]
        out.append(f"## {arch} {cond}  ({r['run_id']})\n")
        out.append(f"artifact_bytes = {osz}; kind = {payload['kind']}\n")
        out.append("| entry | file_size | compress_size | compress_type |")
        out.append("|---|---|---|---|")
        z = zipfile.ZipFile(p)
        for i in z.infolist():
            out.append(f"| OUT {i.filename} | {i.file_size} | {i.compress_size} | {i.compress_type} |")
        if "pickled" in st:
            zi = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(st["pickled"]))
            for i in zi.infolist():
                out.append(f"| IN {i.filename} | {i.file_size} | {i.compress_size} | {i.compress_type} |")
        out.append("")
open("results/artifact_zip_listing.md","w").write("\n".join(out))
print("wrote results/artifact_zip_listing.md")
EOF

import io, zipfile, os, json, sys, re
sys.path.insert(0, "code")
import torch
torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

ART = "results/precision_artifacts"

runs = [json.loads(l) for l in open("results/runs.jsonl") if l.strip()]
sel_rows = {}
for r in runs:
    if r.get("part")=="C" and r.get("phase")=="factorial" and r.get("status")=="ok" \
       and (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python","").startswith("3.12"):
        k = (r["architecture"], r["method"])
        sel_rows[k] = r

def inner_pkl_keys(pickled):
    zi = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(pickled))
    pkl = zi.read([n for n in zi.namelist() if n.endswith("data.pkl")][0])
    # count literal key strings 'data/N' (persistent_id tuples store the key as a str)
    keys = {}
    for m in re.finditer(rb'X(\\x01|\\x02)\\x00\\x00\\x00([0-9]{1,2})\\x00', pkl):
        pass
    # simpler: the key appears as SHORT_BINUNICODE 'N' — count via memo strings
    import pickletools
    strs = []
    try:
        for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(pkl):
            if op.name in ("SHORT_BINUNICODE","BINUNICODE") and isinstance(arg,str) and arg.isdigit():
                strs.append((arg,pos))
    except Exception as e:
        pass
    return strs, pkl

for arch in ("mlp","cnn","gcn"):
    for cond in ("dense_int8","sparse_int8"):
        r = sel_rows.get((arch, cond))
        p = r["artifact"]
        payload = torch.load(p, weights_only=False)
        st = payload["state"]
        if "pickled" not in st:
            continue
        pkl = None
        zi = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(st["pickled"]))
        pkl = zi.read([n for n in zi.namelist() if n.endswith("data.pkl")][0])
        strs = []
        import pickletools
        try:
            for op, arg, pos in pickletools.genops(pkl):
                if op.name in ("SHORT_BINUNICODE","BINUNICODE") and isinstance(arg,str) and arg.isdigit():
                    strs.append((arg,pos))
        except Exception:
            pass
        print(f"=== {arch} {cond}: pkl len={len(pkl)}")
        print("   numeric short-strings (possible storage keys):", strs)
        # find where the first _rebuild_tensor_v2 / _rebuild_qtensor pid tuple starts
        i = pkl.find(b"QInt8Storage")
        print("   QInt8Storage at", i, "ctx:", repr(pkl[max(0,i-60):i+60]))
EOF

if r.get("phase") == "factorial":

    # C3: the C2 int8 rows are superseded (their int8 accounting was blind to the
    # quantized weights). Drop them from the selection so C3 int8 rows win.
    c2_int8_run_ids = set()
    for r in runs:
        if (r.get("part") == "C" and r.get("status") == "ok"
                and "int8" in (r.get("method") or "")
                and (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "").startswith("3.12")
                and "c3" not in (r.get("run_id") or "")):
            # C2 rows were written 2026-11-10T00:3x; C3 rows are later. Identify
            # C2 int8 rows by their (phase, arch, method) + pre-C3 timestamp.
            c2_int8_run_ids.add(r["run_id"])
    # Actually: keep the C2 int8 rows in the *superseded* narrative but exclude
    # them from the latest_ok selection. We do this by dropping rows whose
    # run_id is in the C2 set AND where a C3 int8 row for the same
    # (phase, arch, method) exists (i.e. they were rerun).
    def _is_superseded_c2_int8(r: dict) -> bool:
        if "int8" not in (r.get("method") or ""):
            return False
        # A C3 int8 row for the same (phase, arch, method) exists later in file
        # order -> this C2 row is superseded.
        for later in runs:
            if later is r:
                break
            if (later.get("part") == "C" and later.get("status") == "ok"
                    and later.get("phase") == r.get("phase")
                    and later.get("architecture") == r.get("architecture")
                    and later.get("method") == r.get("method")
                    and "int8" in (later.get("method") or "")
                    and later["run_id"] != r["run_id"]
                    and "20261110" in later["run_id"]
                    and (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "").startswith("3.12")):
                # later is a C3 row only if it was written after the C2 row
                # (file order in runs.jsonl == write order). Since we iterate
                # runs in file order, `later` appears after `r`.
                return True
        return False

    prec_rows_c3 = {}
    fact_rows_c3 = {}
    for arch, rows in prec_rows.items():
        prec_rows_c3[arch] = [r for r in rows if not _is_superseded_c2_int8(r)]
    for arch, rows in fact_rows.items():
        fact_rows_c3[arch] = [r for r in rows if not _is_superseded_c2_int8(r)]

    # latest ok row per (arch, fmt) for the standalone table
    def latest_ok(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, dict]:
        out: dict[str, dict] = {}
        for r in rows:
            if r.get("status") == "ok":
                out[r["method"]] = r  # file order: last ok wins (C3 after C2)
        return out

    out = []

content.text:
# Lab 3 `results/runs.jsonl` record schema

Every command (`train`, `eval`, `bench`) appends exactly one JSON object per
attempted run to `results/runs.jsonl` (append-only: lines are never edited or
deleted; a corrected re-bench adds a new line whose `supersedes` lists the
earlier, now-incorrect run_ids). This file documents the fields.

## Identity / linkage

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | str | Unique id for this record: `<arch>-<method>-<UTC timestamp>-<shortuuid>`. |
| `status` | str | `"ok"` or `"failed"`. |
| `reason` | str/null | Failure reason when `status == "failed"`. |
| `part` | str | `"A"` (dense reference). |
| `phase` | str/null | Matrix phase the record belongs to: `"pilot"` for the Part B pilot matrix (seed 0, including the B.6 `dense_ft` control arms) and `"confirm"` for the confirmatory reruns (seeds 1/2/3, B.3). **B2 (2026-11-09, before any pilot-matrix run):** every new Part B record carries `phase`; all earlier records (Part A, and the B1/B1b Part B smoke rows) predate the field and carry `null` in any record written by new code, or no field at all (never edited — the log is append-only). |
| `architecture` | str | `mlp` / `cnn` / `gcn`. |
| `method` | str | `"dense"` for the Part A baseline. |
| `seed` | int | Random seed. |
| `command` | str | `train` / `eval` / `bench`. |
| `parent_run_id` | str/null | For `bench` (and `eval`), the `run_id` of the **training run** that produced the checkpoint being benchmarked. Carried from the checkpoint metadata `run_id`. |
| `supersedes` | list[str] | For a corrected re-bench: the `run_id`s of the earlier bench records for the same (architecture, seed) that are now known to be incorrect (e.g. A1's wrong MAC/byte figures). The old lines remain in the log untouched. |

## Training / selection

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `train_epochs` | int/null | Epochs actually run (may stop early). |
| `finetune_epochs` | int | 0 in Part A. |
| `best_epoch` | int/null | Epoch of the validation-selected checkpoint. |
| `val_acc`, `val_loss` | float/null | Validation accuracy / loss. |
| `test_acc` | float/null | Test accuracy (evaluated only on the selected checkpoint). |

## Size

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `total_params` | int | `sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())`. |
| `nonzero_params` | int | Number of nonzero weight/param elements. For the dense baseline this equals `total_params`; Part B arms report the physically sparse count. |
| `dense_bytes` | int | **Actual on-disk size** (bytes) of a `torch.save(state_dict)` file — the bare state dict (no metadata) written to a temp file, read with `os.path.getsize`. Includes the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead, so it is slightly larger than `raw_tensor_bytes`. |
| `raw_tensor_bytes` | int | `sum(t.numel() * t.element_size())` over every state_dict tensor — pure payload bytes, no container overhead. |
| `gzip_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** gzip-9 size (bytes) of the `dense_bytes` state_dict file. Reported for **every run, dense included** — it is a property of the dense container, not of a compression method. Null only where a run failed before measuring it. |
| `compressed_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** RESERVED for the **compact-export artifact** (Part B path 2: the genuinely sparse on-disk file — S2 rebuilt dense model, S1/S3 CSR file, S4 packed N:M file). **Null for the dense Part A baseline** (dense has no compact export). Part A `bench` rows record the gzip-9 figure in `gzip_bytes`, not here. |

### Part B (sparsity) additions (Task B1)

Pruning arms (`command == "prune"`, `part == "B"`) append **two rows per arm**,
`stage="post_prune"` and `stage="post_finetune"`, sharing one `arm_id`.
(The pilot driver `uv run python -m lab3 pilot` appends exactly these rows with
`phase="pilot"`, seed 0, one per cell of {mlp,cnn,gcn} x {s1,s2,s3,s4} x
{0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9} plus one `dense_ft` control arm (target 0) per architecture;
failed arms additionally append `stage="failed"` rows. Progress: one line per
arm in `results/pilot_log.txt`; summaries: `results/pilot_summary.csv` (one line
per arm x stage) and `results/pilot_per_layer.csv` (arm, stage, per tensor).)

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `part` | str | `"B"`. |
| `command` | str | `prune`. |
| `stage` | str | `post_prune` / `post_finetune`. |
| `arm_id` | str | Shared by the arm's two rows: `<arch>-<method>-t<target>-seed<seed>-<UTC ts>-<uuid6>`. |
| `method` | str | `s1` / `s2` / `s3` / `s4`. |
| `target_sparsity` | float | Frozen target (0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9). |
| `achieved_sparsity` | float | Fraction of **eligible weight** elements that are zero (post_prune / post_finetune each). |
| `achieved_param_sparsity` | float | Fraction of **all dense params** that are zero (includes biases and, for S2, the rebuilt model's smaller param total). |
| `nm_pattern` | str/null | S4 only, e.g. `"2:4"`. |
| `group_sparsity` | float/null | S2 only: fraction of groups removed (the frozen target's group fraction). |
| `parent_run_id` | str | The **canonical seed-0 dense training run** for this architecture (from the checkpoint metadata). |
| `checkpoint` | str/null | Path of the saved pruned post-finetune model, `checkpoints/pilot/<arm_id>.pt` (set on both rows; file exists once the run completes). |
| `per_layer` | list[dict] | One entry per eligible tensor: `name`, `shape` (dense parent shape for S1/S3/S4; rebuilt shape for S2), `numel`, `nonzero`, `sparsity`. |
| `paths` | dict | Two runtime paths (B.4), keyed `dense_zeros` and `compact`: `runtime_status` (`ok` / `unsupported:<reason>` / `dense_fallback:<reason>`), `latency` (frozen protocol), `rss_before_model_bytes`, `peak_rss_bytes`, `model_rss_delta_bytes`, and the path's size fields: `dense_zeros` → `dense_bytes` + `gzip_bytes`; `compact` → `compressed_bytes` (the compact artifact file size) and `artifact` (path). For S4 the `dense_zeros` row is the benchmarked dense fallback when the semi-structured runtime is unsupported; see `paths.compact.runtime_status`. |

`status=failed` rows carry a classified `reason`: `unsupported_backend`,
`numerical`, `bug`, `not_applicable` (plus the exception message after `:`).

## Compute (MAC estimates)

Computed from the actual model's layer shapes (works for any
Linear/Conv2d/GCNConv sizes), not hard-coded. Per single sample (per image /
per node for fmnist-MLP/CNN; full graph for GCN).

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `est_macs` | int | Total forward MACs assuming **all weights are nonzero** (dense convention). |
| `est_macs_nonzero` | int | Same count but only over weight elements that are **actually nonzero** in the loaded checkpoint. Equals `est_macs` for the dense baseline; smaller once Part B prunes weights. |
| `est_macs_sparse_input` | int/null | GCN only: `est_macs` with the layer-1 projection counted as `nnz(X) * out` instead of `N * in * out`, because Cora's node features are ~1.3% dense (sparse-input convention). Null for MLP/CNN. |
| `gcn_norm_macs` | int/null | GCN only: the degree-normalization (D^{1/2}) elementwise scaling multiplications, `2 * out * (E + N)` per GCNConv layer, reported **separately** and excluded from `est_macs`. Null for MLP/CNN. |

### MAC conventions

- **Linear(in, out):** `in * out` per token (1 per image / per node). Bias excluded.
- **Conv2d(cin, cout, k, padding):** `cin * cout * k^2 * H_out * W_out` per image
  (`H_out`/`W_out` are the actual output feature-map dims after padding). MaxPool/ReLU contribute 0.
- **GCNConv(in, out)** (torch_geometric, self-loops added): the weight is applied **once per
  node** (`X @ W`), not per edge. Per layer:
  - projection = `N * in * out` (dense-X weight product),
  - aggregation = `(E + N) * out` (weighted sum over the E directed edges plus N self-loops).
  - `est_macs` = sum over layers of (projection + aggregation); normalization scales go in `gcn_norm_macs`.
  - `est_macs_sparse_input` = `est_macs` but with the layer-1 projection replaced by `nnz(X) * out`.
  - For Cora: N = 2,708, E = 10,556, in1 = 1,433, out1 = 16, in2 = 16, out2 = 7 →
    `est_macs` ≈ 6.27e7, `est_macs_nonzero` = `est_macs` (dense),
    `est_macs_sparse_input` ≈ 1.0e6.

### Dense seed-0 reference values

- MLP: `est_macs` = 234,752 per image.
- CNN: `est_macs` = 1,697,280 per image (conv2 output is 10×10: 28 → conv1 pad2 → 28 →
  pool → 14 → conv2 5×5 no pad → 10 → pool → 5).

## Memory

Measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports torch + loads the **small fixed
benchmark input** (never the 55k training tensor), records `rss_before_model_bytes`,
(2) loads the checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording the peak.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rss_before_model_bytes` | int | RSS after imports + benchmark-input load, **before** loading the model. |
| `peak_rss_bytes` | int | Peak RSS observed while loading the model and running forwards. |
| `model_rss_delta_bytes` | int | `peak_rss_bytes - rss_before_model_bytes` — the memory attributable to the model + activations. |

## Latency

Frozen protocol: `torch.inference_mode()`, `model.eval()`, 20 warm-up + 200 timed
iterations, `time.perf_counter_ns`, median and IQR reported. Inputs are the fixed
**benchmark batch** (first 256 TEST images, inputs only) — not training images.

`latency` is a dict keyed by `batch_1` / `batch_256` (fmnist) or `full_graph` (gcn),
each with: `median_ms`, `iqr_ms`, `warmup`, `iters`, `threads`, `batch_size`.

## Provenance

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `wall_time_s` | float | Wall-clock seconds for the command. |
| `code_hash` | str | SHA-256 over all files under `code/` (git-free). |
| `versions` | dict | python / torch / numpy / platform versions. |
| `timestamp` | str | ISO-8601 UTC creation time. |
| `target_sparsity`, `achieved_sparsity`, `stored_precision`, `compute_precision`, `accumulator_precision` | — | 0.0 / "fp32" for the dense baseline. |

## Fixed benchmark input

`results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt` = first 256 TEST Fashion-MNIST images,
inputs only (no labels), saved once. `results/bench/cora_bench_input.pt` = full-graph
Cora features + edge_index. These are the latency/RSS inputs and are independent of

attempted run to `results/runs.jsonl` (append-only: lines are never edited or
deleted; a corrected re-bench adds a new line whose `supersedes` lists the
earlier, now-incorrect run_ids). This file documents the fields.

## Identity / linkage

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | str | Unique id for this record: `<arch>-<method>-<UTC timestamp>-<shortuuid>`. |
| `status` | str | `"ok"` or `"failed"`. |
| `reason` | str/null | Failure reason when `status == "failed"`. |
| `part` | str | `"A"` (dense reference). |
| `phase` | str/null | Matrix phase the record belongs to: `"pilot"` for the Part B pilot matrix (seed 0, including the B.6 `dense_ft` control arms) and `"confirm"` for the confirmatory reruns (seeds 1/2/3, B.3). **B2 (2026-11-09, before any pilot-matrix run):** every new Part B record carries `phase`; all earlier records (Part A, and the B1/B1b Part B smoke rows) predate the field and carry `null` in any record written by new code, or no field at all (never edited — the log is append-only). |
| `architecture` | str | `mlp` / `cnn` / `gcn`. |
| `method` | str | `"dense"` for the Part A baseline. |
| `seed` | int | Random seed. |
| `command` | str | `train` / `eval` / `bench`. |
| `parent_run_id` | str/null | For `bench` (and `eval`), the `run_id` of the **training run** that produced the checkpoint being benchmarked. Carried from the checkpoint metadata `run_id`. |
| `supersedes` | list[str] | For a corrected re-bench: the `run_id`s of the earlier bench records for the same (architecture, seed) that are now known to be incorrect (e.g. A1's wrong MAC/byte figures). The old lines remain in the log untouched. |

## Training / selection

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `train_epochs` | int/null | Epochs actually run (may stop early). |
| `finetune_epochs` | int | 0 in Part A. |
| `best_epoch` | int/null | Epoch of the validation-selected checkpoint. |
| `val_acc`, `val_loss` | float/null | Validation accuracy / loss. |
| `test_acc` | float/null | Test accuracy (evaluated only on the selected checkpoint). |

## Size

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `total_params` | int | `sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())`. |
| `nonzero_params` | int | Number of nonzero weight/param elements. For the dense baseline this equals `total_params`; Part B arms report the physically sparse count. |
| `dense_bytes` | int | **Actual on-disk size** (bytes) of a `torch.save(state_dict)` file — the bare state dict (no metadata) written to a temp file, read with `os.path.getsize`. Includes the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead, so it is slightly larger than `raw_tensor_bytes`. |
| `raw_tensor_bytes` | int | `sum(t.numel() * t.element_size())` over every state_dict tensor — pure payload bytes, no container overhead. |
| `gzip_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** gzip-9 size (bytes) of the `dense_bytes` state_dict file. Reported for **every run, dense included** — it is a property of the dense container, not of a compression method. Null only where a run failed before measuring it. |
| `compressed_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** RESERVED for the **compact-export artifact** (Part B path 2: the genuinely sparse on-disk file — S2 rebuilt dense model, S1/S3 CSR file, S4 packed N:M file). **Null for the dense Part A baseline** (dense has no compact export). Part A `bench` rows record the gzip-9 figure in `gzip_bytes`, not here. |

### Part B (sparsity) additions (Task B1)

Pruning arms (`command == "prune"`, `part == "B"`) append **two rows per arm**,
`stage="post_prune"` and `stage="post_finetune"`, sharing one `arm_id`.
(The pilot driver `uv run python -m lab3 pilot` appends exactly these rows with
`phase="pilot"`, seed 0, one per cell of {mlp,cnn,gcn} x {s1,s2,s3,s4} x
{0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9} plus one `dense_ft` control arm (target 0) per architecture;
failed arms additionally append `stage="failed"` rows. Progress: one line per
arm in `results/pilot_log.txt`; summaries: `results/pilot_summary.csv` (one line
per arm x stage) and `results/pilot_per_layer.csv` (arm, stage, per tensor).)

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `part` | str | `"B"`. |
| `command` | str | `prune`. |
| `stage` | str | `post_prune` / `post_finetune`. |
| `arm_id` | str | Shared by the arm's two rows: `<arch>-<method>-t<target>-seed<seed>-<UTC ts>-<uuid6>`. |
| `method` | str | `s1` / `s2` / `s3` / `s4`. |
| `target_sparsity` | float | Frozen target (0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9). |
| `achieved_sparsity` | float | Fraction of **eligible weight** elements that are zero (post_prune / post_finetune each). |
| `achieved_param_sparsity` | float | Fraction of **all dense params** that are zero (includes biases and, for S2, the rebuilt model's smaller param total). |
| `nm_pattern` | str/null | S4 only, e.g. `"2:4"`. |
| `group_sparsity` | float/null | S2 only: fraction of groups removed (the frozen target's group fraction). |
| `parent_run_id` | str | The **canonical seed-0 dense training run** for this architecture (from the checkpoint metadata). |
| `checkpoint` | str/null | Path of the saved pruned post-finetune model, `checkpoints/pilot/<arm_id>.pt` (set on both rows; file exists once the run completes). |
| `per_layer` | list[dict] | One entry per eligible tensor: `name`, `shape` (dense parent shape for S1/S3/S4; rebuilt shape for S2), `numel`, `nonzero`, `sparsity`. |
| `paths` | dict | Two runtime paths (B.4), keyed `dense_zeros` and `compact`: `runtime_status` (`ok` / `unsupported:<reason>` / `dense_fallback:<reason>`), `latency` (frozen protocol), `rss_before_model_bytes`, `peak_rss_bytes`, `model_rss_delta_bytes`, and the path's size fields: `dense_zeros` → `dense_bytes` + `gzip_bytes`; `compact` → `compressed_bytes` (the compact artifact file size) and `artifact` (path). `status=failed` rows carry a classified `reason`: `unsupported_backend`,
`numerical`, `bug`, `not_applicable` (plus the exception message after `:`).

## Compute (MAC estimates)

Computed from the actual model's layer shapes (works for any
Linear/Conv2d/GCNConv sizes), not hard-coded. Per single sample (per image /
per node for fmnist-MLP/CNN; full graph for GCN).

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `est_macs` | int | Total forward MACs assuming **all weights are nonzero** (dense convention). |
| `est_macs_nonzero` | int | Same count but only over weight elements that are **actually nonzero** in the loaded checkpoint. Equals `est_macs` for the dense baseline; smaller once Part B prunes weights. |
| `est_macs_sparse_input` | int/null | GCN only: `est_macs` with the layer-1 projection counted as `nnz(X) * out` instead of `N * in * out`, because Cora's node features are ~1.3% dense (sparse-input convention). Null for MLP/CNN. |

- **Linear(in, out):** `in * out` per token (1 per image / per node). Bias excluded.

  - `est_macs_sparse_input` = `est_macs` but with the layer-1 projection replaced by `nnz(X) * out`.
  - For Cora: N = 2,708, E = 10,556, in1 = 1,433, out1 = 16, in2 = 16, out2 = 7 →
    `est_macs` ≈ 6.27e7, `est_macs_nonzero` = `est_macs` (dense),
    `est_macs_sparse_input` ≈ 1.0e6.

- MLP: `est_macs` = 234,752 per image.
- CNN: `est_macs` = 1,697,280 per image (conv2 output is 10×10: 28 → conv1 pad2 → 28 →
  pool → 14 → conv2 5×5 no pad → 10 → pool → 5).

## Memory

Measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports torch + loads the **small fixed
benchmark input** (never the 55k training tensor), records `rss_before_model_bytes`,
(2) loads the checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording the peak.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rss_before_model_bytes` | int | RSS after imports + benchmark-input load, **before** loading the model. |
| `peak_rss_bytes` | int | Peak RSS observed while loading the model and running forwards. |
| `model_rss_delta_bytes` | int | `peak_rss_bytes - rss_before_model_bytes` — the memory attributable to the model + activations. |

## Latency

Frozen protocol: `torch.inference_mode()`, `model.eval()`, 20 warm-up + 200 timed

each with: `median_ms`, `iqr_ms`, `warmup`, `iters`, `threads`, `batch_size`.

## Provenance

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `wall_time_s` | float | Wall-clock seconds for the command. |
| `code_hash` | str | SHA-256 over all files under `code/` (git-free). |
| `versions` | dict | python / torch / numpy / platform versions. |
| `timestamp` | str | ISO-8601 UTC creation time. |
| `target_sparsity`, `achieved_sparsity`, `stored_precision`, `compute_precision`, `accumulator_precision` | — | 0.0 / "fp32" for the dense baseline. |

## Fixed benchmark input

`results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt` = first 256 TEST Fashion-MNIST images,
inputs only (no labels), saved once. `results/bench/cora_bench_input.pt` = full-graph
Cora features + edge_index. These are the latency/RSS inputs and are independent of
the 55k training tensor.

| `gcn_norm_macs` | int/null | GCN only: the degree-normalization (D^{1/2}) elementwise scaling multiplications, `2 * out * (E + N)` per GCNConv layer, reported **separately** and excluded from `est_macs`. Null for MLP/CNN. |

### MAC conventions

- **Linear(in, out):** `in * out` per token (1 per image / per node). Bias excluded.
- **Conv2d(cin, cout, k, padding):** `cin * cout * k^2 * H_out * W_out` per image
  (`H_out`/`W_out` are the actual output feature-map dims after padding). MaxPool/ReLU contribute 0.
- **GCNConv(in, out)** (torch_geometric, self-loops added): the weight is applied **once per
  node** (`X @ W`), not per edge. Per layer:
  - projection = `N * in * out` (dense-X weight product),
  - aggregation = `(E + N) * out` (weighted sum over the E directed edges plus N self-loops).
  - `est_macs` = sum over layers of (projection + aggregation); normalization scales go in `gcn_norm_macs`.
  - `est_macs_sparse_input` = `est_macs` but with the layer-1 projection replaced by `nnz(X) * out`.
  - For Cora: N = 2,708, E = 10,556, in1 = 1,433, out1 = 16, in2 = 16, out2 = 7 →
    `est_macs` ≈ 6.27e7, `est_macs_nonzero` = `est_macs` (dense),
    `est_macs_sparse_input` ≈ 1.0e6.

### Dense seed-0 reference values

- MLP: `est_macs` = 234,752 per image.
- CNN: `est_macs` = 1,697,280 per image (conv2 output is 10×10: 28 → conv1 pad2 → 28 →
  pool → 14 → conv2 5×5 no pad → 10 → pool → 5).

## Memory

Measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports torch + loads the **small fixed
benchmark input** (never the 55k training tensor), records `rss_before_model_bytes`,
(2) loads the checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording the peak.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rss_before_model_bytes` | int | RSS after imports + benchmark-input load, **before** loading the model. |
| `peak_rss_bytes` | int | Peak RSS observed while loading the model and running forwards. |
| `model_rss_delta_bytes` | int | `peak_rss_bytes - rss_before_model_bytes` — the memory attributable to the model + activations. |

## Latency

Frozen protocol: `torch.inference_mode()`, `model.eval()`, 20 warm-up + 200 timed
iterations, `time.perf_counter_ns`, median and IQR reported. Inputs are the fixed
**benchmark batch** (first 256 TEST images, inputs only) — not training images.

each with: `median_ms`, `iqr_ms`, `warmup`, `iters`, `threads`, `batch_size`.

inputs only (no labels), saved once. `results/bench/cora_bench_input.pt` = full-graph
Cora features + edge_index. These are the latency/RSS inputs and are independent of
the 55k training tensor.

def run_precision(arch: str | None = None) -> list:
    archs = (arch,) if arch else ARCHS
    out = []
    set_threads()
    P.set_qnnpack_engine()
    for a in archs:
        parent = dense_parent(a)
        prid = _parent_run_id(a)
        for fmt in FORMATS:
            print(f"[precision] {a} {fmt}", flush=True)
            rec = P.convert_and_measure(a, fmt, parent, prid, write=True)
            print(f"   status={rec.get('status')} val_acc={rec.get('val_acc')} "
                  f"nonzero={rec.get('nonzero_params')} "
                  f"frac_macs={rec.get('frac_macs_reduced_precision')} "
                  f"artifact_bytes={rec.get('artifact_bytes')} "
                  f"reload={rec.get('reload_equivalence')}", flush=True)
            out.append(rec)
    return out

    return out

+    quantized projection weights). Re-runs:

+      - dense_int8 + sparse_int8 factorial conditions for each arch
+        (phase="factorial", using the C2-selected int8 method per arch from
+        int8_selection.json).

+    The selection is recomputed from the NEW precision rows; the caller writes
+    it to results/int8_selection.json.

+    prec_out = []

"""Part C — reduced precision (predictions.md C.1-C.3, frozen).

Conversions from the canonical seed-0 dense FP32 parent, per architecture:
fp16, bf16, dynamic INT8, static INT8 (calibrated), simulated weight-only INT4.

Backend facts on THIS machine (Apple M4 Pro, torch 2.15.0, darwin), probed in
Task C1b and recorded in results/precision_support.md:

* ``torch.backends.quantized.supported_engines == ['qnnpack']``;
  ``torch._C._get_qengine() == 2`` (QNNPACK only; fbgemm/onednn absent).
* ``torch.ao.quantization.quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear}, dtype=torch.qint8)``
  works and produces native quantized Linear modules that execute the qnnpack
  ``quantized::linear`` kernel (weight INT8 per-tensor symmetric, activation
  quantized per-batch at runtime). Same for ``{nn.Conv2d}``.
* FX static flow: ``prepare_fx``/``convert_fx`` with
  ``get_default_qconfig_mapping("qnnpack")`` works for Linear and Conv2d
  (produces ``LinearReLU`` / ``ConvReLU2d`` fused quantized modules).
  PT2E (``torch.ao.quantization.quantize_pt2e``) does NOT exist in torch 2.15;
  torchao is not installed (not added — not needed).
* ``nn.Linear`` and ``nn.Conv2d`` execute natively in fp16 and bf16 on CPU
  (output dtype == input dtype; no upcast).
* GCNConv (PyG propagate / scatter) has no quantized or half-precision kernel;
  only its inner projection ``GCNConv.lin`` (an ``nn.Linear``) can run reduced
  precision. Reduced-precision GCN rows therefore record that the projection
  ran reduced precision and the aggregation/normalization ran fp32.

INT8 methods (native qnnpack kernels):
- Dynamic: ``quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear}, dtype=torch.qint8)`` — INT8 weights,
  per-batch activation quantization, qnnpack ``quantized::linear`` kernel.
- Static (calibrated): FX ``prepare_fx``/``convert_fx`` with the qnnpack qconfig
  mapping, calibrated on the frozen calibration inputs (C.1 rule).
  Activation qparams are fixed at calibration time.

Simulated weight-only INT4 (frozen C.1):
- Per-output-channel symmetric quantization to [-8, 7], fp32 scale per output
  channel, 2 values packed per uint8 on disk.
- Dequantize to fp32 and compute in fp32. **The dequantization is INSIDE the
  timed region** (decided once, applied identically to every INT4 run).
  ``runtime_status = "simulated_non_native"``.
"""

Per-entry `zipfile.ZipFile(artifact).infolist()` for the 12 latest-ok

3.12 factorial artifacts. `file_size` = stored (uncompressed) bytes;

`compress_size` = bytes on disk; `compress_type` 0 = stored (no

compression). `OUT` entries are the outer .pt zip (torch.save of

`{kind, architecture, state}`); `IN` entries are the inner zip of the

`state['pickled']` bytes for the mlp/gcn int8 rows (torch.save(model)

re-archives the whole module tree; for cnn static the state is a flat

state dict, so there is no inner zip). See C3_DONE.md issue 2 for the

explanation of the dense-vs-sparse artifact_bytes gap.

## mlp dense_fp32  (mlp-dense-20261110T003408250547Z-844c70)

   quantize-dequantize (MLP 0.8914, CNN 0.9006, GCN 0.7860).

   file, and `artifact_bytes` is now the real file size.

   params. C2 reports the nonzero count of the integer weight representation

   produces exactly 12 conditions (3 archs × 4 conditions), all `status=ok`.

## C3 — superseded C2 INT8 rows (integer-weight accounting blind to quantized projections)

C3 (2026-11-10T01:30 UTC) re-ran **only the INT8 records** as new rows because the
C2 integer-weight accounting (`int8_nonzero` / `bytes_by_dtype` /
`nonzero_after_int8`) was **blind to the quantized projection weights**. The C2
traversal matched only modules whose `_packed_params` child exposed a working
`_weight_bias()`, so it missed the two FX-static shapes produced by `convert_fx`:
(a) GCN per-projection GraphModules with a raw `_packed_weight_N`
`torch.ScriptObject` (class `torch.classes.quantized.LinearPackedParamsBase`,
which exposes `unpack()` but NOT `_weight_bias`), and (b) CNN static convs whose
`_packed_params` is a raw ScriptObject attached directly to the Conv2d module
(not a Python LinearPackedParams wrapper child).

**Symptom in the C2 rows** (the bug the reviewer flagged):
- gcn `dense_int8` / `sparse_int8`: `nonzero_after_int8 = 23` (the 16+7 GCN
  biases, NOT the 22,928+112 projection weights) and
  `bytes_by_dtype = {"fp32": 92}` (biases only) — even though val acc
  (0.794–0.796) proved the INT8 weights were present and executing.
- The standalone gcn `int8_dynamic` / `int8_static` rows were affected the same
  way (nonzero_params = 23, bytes_by_dtype = {fp32: 184/200}).
- CNN dynamic-INT8 also under-counted (it quantizes the fc layers but the convs
  stay fp32 under the frozen C.1 `quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear})` spec, so the
  C2 count of 103,680 was actually correct for the linear-only subset; C3 keeps
  the same value but now derives it from the working traversal).

C3 fixes `_int_weight_tensors` / `bytes_by_dtype` / `int8_nonzero` to use a
`_qnnpack_weight_bias` helper that handles both shapes (Python-wrapper
`_weight_bias` path + raw-ScriptObject `unpack()` path), deduplicates the
LinearPackedParams wrapper module (whose `vars()` hold the same ScriptObject as
its parent's `_packed_params`, which would otherwise double-count), and adds a
buffer-aware fallback (the C2 fallback only iterated `named_parameters`, which
double-counted the INT4 `packed` uint8 buffer as 'uint8').
